lesson.title: Choose a plan
lesson.scenario: Fattoush and Knafeh are planning tomorrow evening. They choose a meal at seven, with tea afterwards. Later practice asks you to adapt when the requested activity changes.

steps.instruction: As Knafeh, suggest making rice and salad for tomorrow.

answers.meaning: Shall we make rice and salad?
Shall we visit my family after work?
answers.rationale: A family visit is possible, but the requested plan is a meal.

answers.arabic: بكرا الساعة ستة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Bukra is-sāʿa sitte nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Tomorrow at six we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: This proposes tea rather than the requested meal.

evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This expression changes or omits a detail requested in this exchange.

steps.instruction: The meal sounds good, but Knafeh has not given a time. Accept and ask when.

prompt.meaning: Shall we make rice and salad?

answers.meaning: And afterwards we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: This adds an activity but leaves the time unanswered.
This accepts the meal and asks for the missing time.
This supplies a time rather than asking for one.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This accepts the meal and asks for the missing time.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This expression changes or omits a detail requested in this exchange.

steps.instruction: Knafeh says seven. Confirm the rice-and-salad plan at that time.

answers.meaning: We’ll make rice and salad at six.
answers.rationale: The meal fits, but six changes the agreed time.

answers.arabic: آه، بكرا الساعة سبعة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Āh, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Yes, tomorrow at seven we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: Seven fits, but tea replaces the meal.

answers.meaning: We’ll make rice and salad at seven.
answers.rationale: Both the meal and seven match the arrangement.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Both the meal and seven match the arrangement.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This expression changes or omits a detail requested in this exchange.

steps.instruction: The meal at seven is agreed. As Knafeh, suggest drinking tea together afterwards.

prompt.meaning: We’ll make rice and salad at seven.

answers.meaning: And afterwards we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: This adds shared tea after the agreed meal.

answers.meaning: And afterwards we’ll make rice and salad.
answers.rationale: This proposes another meal instead of tea.

answers.arabic: بكرا الساعة ستة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Bukra is-sāʿa sitte nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Tomorrow at six we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: This moves tea to six rather than adding it afterwards.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This adds shared tea after the agreed meal.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This expression changes or omits a detail requested in this exchange.

steps.instruction: New arrangement: Fattoush asks what you will do tomorrow. Propose only tea together at six.

answers.meaning: We’ll make rice and salad at six.
answers.rationale: The day can be understood, but this changes tea into a meal.

answers.arabic: بكرا الساعة ستة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Bukra is-sāʿa sitte nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Tomorrow at six we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: This gives the requested day, time and shared drink.

answers.arabic: اليوم الساعة ستة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Il-yōm is-sāʿa sitte nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Today at six we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: The activity and time fit, but this changes tomorrow to today.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This gives the requested day, time and shared drink.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This expression changes or omits a detail requested in this exchange.

steps.instruction: New arrangement: agree to tea together tomorrow at seven.

answers.arabic: بكرا الساعة ستة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Bukra is-sāʿa sitte nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Tomorrow at six we’ll drink tea together.
We’ll make rice and salad at seven.
answers.rationale: This changes tea into rice and salad.

answers.arabic: آه، بكرا الساعة سبعة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Āh, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Yes, tomorrow at seven we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: This agrees to the requested tea plan at seven tomorrow.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This agrees to the requested tea plan at seven tomorrow.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This expression changes or omits a detail requested in this exchange.
evaluation.retryHint: Keep the new details, not the earlier six-o’clock plan.

introduction.goal: Propose a meal, ask for a time, and distinguish a meal plan from a tea plan.

line.meaning: Shall we make rice and salad?
We’ll make rice and salad at seven.
And afterwards we’ll drink tea together.

expressions.meaning: Shall we make rice and salad?
We’ll make rice and salad at seven.
And afterwards we’ll drink tea together.

introduction.usageNote: Build the arrangement in turns: suggest an activity, ask for the time, then confirm. Read each practice situation: a later request can change the plan.
introduction.dialectNote: Urban Palestinian teaching target; transliteration remains available. Urban coffee pronunciation and address forms follow the first-unit model. Ahlak addresses Knafeh; ahli refers to the speaker’s own family. The scenes share an evening setting; these phrases do not teach how to distinguish morning from evening. No Jordanian variants or native-expert review claimed. ā/ī/ū and ē/ō mark long vowels; ʿ = ع, ḥ = ح, ʾ = glottal stop.
introduction.recordingNote: No reviewed recordings. Dialogue and prompt text are draft recording scripts. Speaker roles are explicit; do not label browser speech as reviewed Palestinian audio. All audio URLs remain null.

teachingCards.title: Propose a meal

phrase.meaning: Shall we make rice and salad?

teachingCards.note: Niʿmal can propose a shared activity in a question. W- joins both foods.

teachingCards.title: Ask for the missing detail
teachingCards.note: Accept the activity with tamām, then ask ayy sāʿa when the time is missing.
teachingCards.recallCue: The meal is agreed, but no time is set. Ask for it.

teachingCards.title: Confirm the meal and time

phrase.meaning: We’ll make rice and salad at seven.

teachingCards.note: Combine the familiar meal with is-sāʿa sabʿa. Tomorrow is already established.
teachingCards.recallCue: Confirm rice and salad at seven.

teachingCards.title: Add what happens next

phrase.meaning: And afterwards we’ll drink tea together.

teachingCards.note: Baʿdēn links tea to the meal already discussed; it does not give a clock time.
teachingCards.recallCue: Add tea together after the meal.

teachingCards.title: Adapt the activity and time

phrase.arabic: بكرا الساعة ستة نشرب شاي سوا.
phrase.arabizi: Bukra is-sāʿa sitte nishrab shāy sawa.
phrase.meaning: Tomorrow at six we’ll drink tea together.

teachingCards.note: Reuse the day/time frame with nishrab shāy sawa. This new arrangement is tea at six.
teachingCards.recallCue: Make a different plan: tea together tomorrow at six.
